# Tidepool Landing Page — Build Plan

**1. Hero** — Two-column split: headline + CTA left, animated product mock right. Sand background (#FAF7F2), deep-teal ink type (#0E3B3B), coral CTA (#FF6B5E). Fraunces display, Inter body. The mock shows a week board filling in like a tide. Copy: "Plan the week together. Then get back to work." Sub: "Tidepool turns Monday chaos into a shared rhythm."

**2. Social proof strip** — Single row of six grayscale fictional team logos. Copy: "Trusted by 4,000+ small teams."

**3. Problem statement** — Full-width, centered, pale seafoam wash. One bold line: "Monday standups shouldn't eat your Monday." Two stat callouts: "31% of the week spent syncing on what to do."

**4. How it works** — Three columns, numbered steps with line illustrations in seafoam on ink circles: Friday close-out (team drops wins/blockers), Sunday draft (Tidepool proposes the week), Monday 15-minute review. Verb-first copy: "Close, draft, align."

**5. Feature bento** — Asymmetric five-card grid on off-white: shared week board, capacity meters, focus blocks, Slack + calendar sync, Friday retros. Cards mix cropped UI screenshots and coral stat chips. Fragment-style copy: "See who's overloaded before it happens."

**6. Testimonial** — Split layout: oversized Fraunces italic pull quote left; photo, name, role right ("We killed our planning meeting. Nobody misses it." — Priya N., studio lead). Seafoam background.

**7. Pricing teaser** — Slim two-plan row: Drift (free, up to 5 seats) and Crew ($8/seat/mo). Ink outlines, minimal chrome, single coral CTA per card.

**8. Final CTA** — Full-bleed deep-teal panel with a subtle wave illustration along the bottom edge. White headline: "Make this week a good one." Email capture button.

**9. Footer** — Sand background, four muted-teal link columns (Product, Teams, Resources, Company), small tide-glyph logo mark.
final:
# Tidepool Landing Page — Revised Plan

**What I'm taking from the reference:** the week-timeline spine (a natural fit for a weekly planner), hand-drawn annotations, and a monospace accent. What I'm leaving: the 60-word run-on headline — our short one is the stronger pattern. Palette keeps its deep-green-plus-coral logic but stays ocean-true: sand (#FAF7F2), deep teal ink (#0B3D3A), coral (#FF6B5E).

**0. Week spine (new)** — Persistent left rail on desktop: vertical timeline with Mon–Sun nodes, monospace day labels. Every section anchors to a day, so the page itself narrates a team's week. Collapses to a horizontal day-strip on mobile.

**1. Hero — Monday node** — Same split layout, same headline: "Plan the week together. Then get back to work." Adopt the hand-drawn arrow from headline to mock, plus one annotation on the mock: circled capacity bar, handwritten note "Maya's overloaded — moved the review to Thu."

**2. Social proof** — Unchanged: six grayscale logos, mono caption "Trusted by 4,000+ small teams."

**3. Problem — Monday node** — Seafoam wash. "Monday standups shouldn't eat your Monday." Stat set as a mono chip: "31% of the week spent syncing on what to do."

**4. How it works — Fri / Sun / Mon nodes** — The three steps now *ride the spine*: Friday close-out, Sunday draft, Monday review. Each gets a hand-drawn circle. Copy stays: "Close, draft, align."

**5. Feature bento — Tue–Thu nodes** — Label the cluster "the deep-work days run themselves." Five asymmetric cards, cropped UI, one coral hand-drawn arrow pointing to Focus Blocks. Fragment copy retained.

**6. Testimonial — Friday node** — Pull quote now in monospace, styled as a typed note pinned to the rail: "We killed our planning meeting. Nobody misses it." — Priya N., studio lead.

**7. Pricing teaser** — Unchanged: Drift (free, 5 seats) and Crew ($8/seat/mo), ink outlines, coral CTAs.

**8. Final CTA — Sunday node** — Deep-teal full bleed, wave edge. Headline now pays off the spine: "Next week starts Sunday night." Email capture.

**9. Footer** — Sand, four muted-teal columns; spine ends on a final node marked "Done ✓" with a hand-drawn check.
